followUps: What would a normal Tuesday look like?
What would we need to start doing now?
shareBack: Offer one picture of your own, kept short, then ask which part of theirs matters most.

line: I don't say it enough: you make me braver than I'd be on my own. When do you feel most like yourself with me?
followUps: What makes those times different?
Is there a time you feel less like yourself?
shareBack: Tell them one moment you felt most yourself with them, then thank them for answering.

line: Is there something you used to be afraid of that you've made peace with?
followUps: What changed for you?
Is there anything that still gets to you?
shareBack: Share one fear of your own that has eased, in a sentence or two, then ask what helped them most.

line: What do you hope I carry forward from you?
followUps: Where did you get that from?
Is there anything you hope I leave behind?
shareBack: Name one thing of theirs you already see in yourself, then ask them to tell you where it started.

line: When you look at who you are now, what part of you comes from how our family did things?
followUps: Is that something you are glad about?
What did you decide to do differently?
shareBack: Offer one piece of the family you see in yourself, in a sentence, then ask about the part they changed.

line: I'd like us to be closer than we've been. What would make that easier for you?
followUps: Is there anything I do that gets in the way?
What did you like about how we used to be?
shareBack: Say one small thing you are willing to do, like calling more often, then ask if that would help.
deliveryCue: Say it somewhere quiet, not in front of the whole family.

line: I want the behind-the-scenes version. What part of getting here was harder than it looked?
followUps: How did you get through that part?
Who helped you most along the way?
shareBack: Say one thing you noticed while they worked toward it, then ask what comes next.

line: Who was the first person you told, and what did they say?
followUps: What was the best reaction you got?
Did anyone surprise you?
shareBack: Tell them how you felt when you heard, in a sentence, then ask how they are going to mark it.

line: I've watched you work toward this for a long time. What's a part of it nobody else got to see?
followUps: When did you start to believe it would happen?
What are you proudest of?
shareBack: Name one moment you remember from their effort, then hand it back with "What else?"

line: I've been telling everyone your news and can't stop grinning. What's the part you're still taking in?
followUps: What did it feel like the moment you knew?
What are you most looking forward to now?
shareBack: Say who you told and how they reacted, in a sentence, then ask how they want to celebrate.

line: I'd love to hear how this came together. Was it a long time coming, or did it surprise you too?
followUps: What was the turning point?
What did you do when you found out?
shareBack: Offer how the news landed for you, in a sentence, then ask what they are most excited about.

line: This deserves more than a quick toast. Start from the beginning, and everyone gets to ask one question.
followUps: Who has the first question?
What was the moment it felt real?
shareBack: Ask your own question last, and keep the spotlight on them rather than on your story.
deliveryCue: Say it once everyone is seated and listening.

line: What's a meal you've had lately that you're still thinking about?
followUps: Where was it?
Would you go back for it, or try to make it yourself?
shareBack: Offer one meal of your own, in a sentence, then ask if they cook much at home.

line: I just started learning to bake bread, and so far it's mostly bricks. Have you picked up anything new lately?
followUps: How did you get into it?
What's been harder than you expected?
shareBack: Say one thing you have learned the hard way so far, then ask what they would tell a beginner.
deliveryCue: Swap in something you have really started lately.

line: Which family get-together do people still talk about? I feel like I missed the good stories.
followUps: Were you there for it?
Who tells it best?
shareBack: Offer one family story you know, kept short, then ask if they have heard a different version.

line: I get the feeling this family has strong opinions about food. Which one is yours?
followUps: Who disagrees with you the most?
Has anyone ever changed your mind?
shareBack: Admit one food opinion of your own, then ask them to settle it.
deliveryCue: Best said at the table, with a smile.

line: What's been on your mind lately, beyond the usual updates? I'd like to actually hear it.
followUps: How long has that been sitting with you?
Is there anything I can do?
shareBack: Offer one thing on your own mind, in a sentence, then go back to theirs.
deliveryCue: Ask when there is time for a real answer, not on the way out the door.

line: Is there anything you're looking forward to these next few months, or anything you're dreading?
followUps: What makes that one stand out?
Is there anything that would make it easier?
shareBack: Name one thing you are looking forward to and one you are not, briefly, then ask how they plan to handle theirs.

line: I usually get the highlights from you. I'd love to hear the rest too, the parts that have been harder.
followUps: What has that been like?
Who have you been able to talk to about it?
shareBack: If they open up, say one hard part of your own season, in a sentence, then ask what would help.

line: We mostly see each other at big gatherings. I'd like to hear how things really are with you lately.
followUps: What has been taking up most of your time?
Is there anything you are looking forward to?
shareBack: Share one honest thing about your own year, in a sentence, then ask about theirs again.
deliveryCue: Say it when it is just the two of you, maybe while helping in the kitchen.

line: Let's go around: what's one thing everyone's hoping for in the next few months?
followUps: What would make that happen?
Can any of us help with it?
shareBack: Go last, keep yours to a sentence, and ask a follow-up of whoever answered most briefly.

line: I'll start: this month has been more stressful than I've let on. Is anyone else carrying something they haven't mentioned?
followUps: What would help with it?
Has anyone been through something similar?
shareBack: Keep your part to a sentence or two, then stay quiet and let others take their time.
deliveryCue: Only if it's true. Keep your part short.

line: What's one thing that would make next month easier for each of you? Maybe we can help each other.
followUps: Who could take that on?
What would make it easier to ask for help?
shareBack: Name one thing that would make your own month easier, then offer to take something on for someone.

line: I came across an old photo of us the other day. Do you remember that trip?
followUps: What do you remember most from it?
Who else was there?
shareBack: Say what you remember about that day in a sentence, then ask if they still have any photos.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real photo or trip, and show it if you have it.

line: What's the best thing that's happened since we last caught up?
followUps: How did that come about?
What's next with it?
shareBack: Offer one good thing from your own last few months, in a sentence, then ask what else they have been up to.

line: It's been too long. Catch me up on the good stuff first. The rest can wait.
followUps: What has been the most fun lately?
Anything coming up you are excited about?
shareBack: Share one good thing from your side, in a sentence, then ask a follow-up about theirs.

line: I've missed you, and I'm sorry I let so much time go by. What's been the biggest thing on your plate since?
followUps: How are you feeling about it?
Is there anything I can help with?
shareBack: Say plainly why you went quiet, in a sentence, with no long excuse, then ask about them again.

line: Now that we've caught up on the news, how have things really been going for you?
followUps: What has been the hardest part?
What has been keeping you going?
shareBack: Offer one honest sentence about your own stretch, then hand it back with a follow-up.

line: I realized I don't know what your days feel like anymore, and I'd like to. What's been good lately, and what's been hard?
followUps: Tell me more about the hard part.
What has been the best part of your week?
shareBack: Describe one day of yours in a sentence or two, then ask what they would change about theirs.

line: How are you holding up with all of it, honestly? You don't have to put on a brave face with me.
followUps: What has been the hardest part?
What would help this week?
shareBack: Skip your own story. Say "That makes sense" and offer one specific thing you can do.
deliveryCue: Ask somewhere private, and be ready to just listen.

line: I keep thinking about what you're going through. Whatever you're feeling about it makes sense to me.
followUps: Do you want to talk about it, or just sit for a bit?
What has been helping, even a little?
shareBack: Offer one specific kind of help, like a meal or a ride, instead of a story of your own.
